questions.question: The thickness of the continental crust beneath the Central Himalayas is of the order of _________ , marking the end of volcanic activity in the region.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**70-72 km**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Central Himalayas** are characterized by one of the thickest continental crusts globally, measuring approximately **70–72 km** in thickness.
 
• This thickness results from the ongoing **tectonic collision between the Indian Plate and the Eurasian Plate**, leading to significant crustal shortening and thickening.
 
• The crustal thickness is indicative of the intense compression and uplift that formed the Himalayas and marked the cessation of volcanic activity in this region.
 
• The **end of volcanic activity** is linked to the crust's inability to facilitate magma ascent due to its exceptional thickness and tectonic configuration.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 Characteristics
 
 
 
 

 Crust
 
 
 
• The uppermost layer over the earth’s surface is called the crust.
 
• It is the thinnest of all the layers.
 
• It is about 35 km. on the continental masses and only 5 km. on the ocean floors.
 
• The main mineral constituents of the continental mass are silica and alumina.
 
• It is thus called sial (si-silica and al-alumina).
 
• The oceanic crust mainly consists of silica and magnesium; it is therefore called sima (si-silica and ma-magnesium)
 
• The crust makes up only 1% of the volume of Earth.
 
 
 
 

 Mantle
 
 
 
• Just beneath the crust is the mantle which extends up to a depth of 2900 km. below the crust.
 
• The mantle is semi-liquid, sort of like a malleable plastic, and makes up 84% of Earth's volume.
 
 
 
 

 Core
 
 
 
• The innermost layer is the core with a radius of about 3500 km.
 
• It is mainly made up of nickel and iron and is called NiFe (Ni – nickel and Fe – ferrous i.e. iron).
 
• The central core has very high temperature and pressure.
 
• The core makes up only 15% of the volume of Earth.

questions.question: The first amendment to the Indian Constitution was made in ________
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__1951.__**

__
 
• The **first amendment Act** was made in **1951.**
 
• The **reasons** for the first amendment were:
 
 
• To remove certain practical difficulties created by the court's decision in several cases such as Kameshwar Singh Case, Romesh Thapar Case, etc.
 
• Issues involved in the cases included freedom of speech, acquisition of the Zamindari land, State monopoly of trade, etc.
 
 
 
• The Constitution (First Amendment) Act, 1951, enacted in 1951, made several changes to the **Fundamental Rights** provisions of the Indian constitution.
 
• It provided against abuse of freedom of speech and expression, **validation of zamindari abolition laws**, and clarified that the right to equality does not bar the enactment of laws that provide "special consideration" for weaker sections of society.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 368** of the Indian Constitution mentions** two types** of amendments to the Indian Constitution:

 
 
• One type of amendment is by a special majority of the Parliament (Lok Sabha & Rajya Sabha).
 
• The second type of amendment is by a special majority of the Parliament with the ratification by half of the total states.

questions.question: What is the main reason behind the substantial rainfall during summer on the western coasts of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Western Ghats**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Western Ghats** are the main reason behind the substantial rainfall during summer on the western coasts of India.
 
• These mountain ranges run parallel to the western coast and act as a barrier to the moisture-laden winds coming from the Arabian Sea.
 
• As these winds ascend the Western Ghats, they cool down, condense, and result in heavy rainfall on the windward side of the mountains.
 
• This phenomenon is known as orographic rainfall and is crucial for the monsoon season in the western coastal regions of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Western Ghats are a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of the eight "hottest hotspots" of biological diversity in the world.
 
• They play a significant role in influencing the climate of the region by intercepting the monsoon winds.
 
• The Western Ghats extend from the state of Gujarat in the north to Tamil Nadu in the south, covering a distance of about 1,600 km.
 
• They are also home to numerous endemic species of flora and fauna, contributing to their ecological importance.

questions.question: What was the capital of North-western province under Ashoka?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Taxila **__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Taxila**

 
 
• **Taxila** was the capital of the **North-western province** under Ashoka's Mauryan Empire.
 
• Located in present-day Pakistan, Taxila was a major center of learning, trade, and culture during ancient times.
 
• It served as a strategic administrative and military hub due to its location on important trade routes.
 
• Ashoka's inscriptions and policies, including the spread of Buddhism, were implemented in Taxila.
 
• The city's significance continued even after the Mauryan Empire, as it remained a prominent center for education and commerce.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ujjayini:**

 
 
• **Ujjayini** (modern-day Ujjain) was the capital of the **Western province** under Ashoka's Mauryan Empire.
 
• It was an important city in ancient India, known for its cultural and religious significance.
 
• Ujjayini was a major center for trade and commerce, located on the trade routes connecting northern and southern India.
 
• It is not associated with the North-western province but played a crucial role in the administration of the Western region.
 
• The city is also mentioned in ancient texts like the Mahabharata and is associated with the legendary king Vikramaditya.
 
 
 
• **Tosali:**
 
 
• **Tosali** was the capital of the **Eastern province** under Ashoka's Mauryan Empire.
 
• Located in present-day Odisha, Tosali was an important administrative center for the region.
 
• Ashoka's rock edicts and inscriptions have been found in this region, indicating its significance during his reign.
 
• Tosali was not associated with the North-western province but played a key role in the governance of the Eastern territories.
 
• The city's exact location is believed to be near modern-day Dhauli, where Ashoka's famous Dhauli Edict is located.
 
 
 
• **Suvarnagiri:**
 
 
• **Suvarnagiri** was the capital of the **Southern province** under Ashoka's Mauryan Empire.
 
• Its name translates to "Golden Mountain," and it was an important administrative and economic center.
 
• Suvarnagiri was located in present-day Karnataka and served as a hub for trade and resource management.
 
• It was not associated with the North-western province but was crucial for the administration of the Southern territories.
 
• The city's strategic location helped Ashoka maintain control over the southern regions of his empire.

questions.question: Which of the following organisations conducts the sample surveys for calculating poverty line in India?

__
 
• The National Sample Survey Office (NSSO) is the organization responsible for conducting sample surveys in India, including those used for calculating the poverty line.
 
• The NSSO operates under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation of the Government of India. It is one of the largest organizations in India conducting sample surveys on various socio-economic aspects of the country.
 
• The NSSO conducts regular household surveys to collect data on various socio-economic indicators, including income, expenditure, employment, and poverty. These surveys involve sampling households across different regions of the country to gather representative data.
 
• The poverty line in India is determined based on the data collected through these sample surveys conducted by the NSSO.
 
• The poverty line is an important benchmark used to assess the extent of poverty and to formulate policies and programs for poverty alleviation in the country.

• It's worth mentioning that the Central Statistics Office (CSO), another organization under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation, is also involved in the compilation and analysis of various statistical data, including national income, economic growth, and other economic indicators. However, when it comes to calculating the poverty line, the primary responsibility lies with the NSSO.
 
• The Ministry of Finance and the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) are not directly involved in conducting sample surveys for calculating the poverty line. However, they may use the data and analysis provided by organizations like the NSSO and CSO for policymaking and economic planning purposes.

__
 
• **The Constitution of India has provisions for the suspension of fundamental rights**, including those under Article 19, during a state of national emergency.
 
• **According to Article 358, the rights conferred by Article 19 can be suspended during the period of a national emergency**.
 
• Under such circumstances, the freedoms under Article 19—including the rights to freedom of speech and to assemble peaceably, among others—are automatically suspended, and the state governments are given more broad powers.
 
• 
 
After the emergency declared in 1975,** the 44th Amendment Act of 1978 introduced protections to prevent the misuse of constitutional emergency provisions**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 356**, often called "President's Rule" or "State Emergency," allows the **President of India to take over the state government's functions if circumstances warrant it.**
 
• **Article 360 **is a provision in the Indian Constitution that **allows the President to proclaim a financial emergency when the country's financial stability or credit is endangered. **
 
• **Article 361** of the Indian Constitution **provides legal protection to the President, Governors, and Rajpramukhs**. According to this article, these individuals are not answerable to any court for executing their duties or any acts done in that performance.

questions.question:
Read the following about the Revenue expenditure.

A. Revenue Expenditure is expenditure incurred for purposes other than the creation of physical or financial assets of the central government.

B. It relates to those expenses incurred for the normal functioning of the government departments and various services, interest payments on debt incurred by the government, and grants given to state governments and other parties (even though some of the grants may be meant for creation of assets).

Identify the INCORRECT statement / statements.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2 (Neither A nor B)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Revenue Expenditure** is expenditure incurred for purposes other than the creation of physical or financial assets of the central government.
 
• It relates to those expenses incurred for the normal functioning of the government departments and various services, interest payments on debt incurred by the government, and grants given to state governments and other parties (even though some of the grants may be meant for creation of assets).
 
• Statement A correctly describes Revenue Expenditure as it is not aimed at creating physical or financial assets.
 
• Statement B correctly explains the components that make up Revenue Expenditure, such as normal functioning expenses, interest payments, and grants to other entities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Revenue Expenditure**

 
 
• Revenue Expenditure is the expenditure that the government incurs for its operational activities and routine functions.
 
• It includes salaries, pensions, interest payments, subsidies, and other routine administrative costs.
 
• This type of expenditure is not intended for the creation of assets but rather for the day-to-day functioning of the government.
 
• It is typically recurrent in nature and is accounted for within the same financial year.
 
 
 
• **Capital Expenditure**
 
 
• Unlike Revenue Expenditure, Capital Expenditure is aimed at creating physical or financial assets.
 
• It includes spending on infrastructure projects, acquisition of machinery, equipment, and other long-term investments.
 
• Capital Expenditure is typically non-recurrent and has a long-term impact on the economy.
 
• It is crucial for economic growth and development as it leads to the creation of assets that generate future economic benefits.
 
 
 
• **Fiscal Deficit**
 
 
• Fiscal Deficit is the difference between the government's total revenue and total expenditure (excluding borrowings) in a given financial year.
 
• It indicates the total borrowing requirements of the government.
 
• A higher fiscal deficit implies greater borrowing and higher interest payments in the future, affecting the country's financial health.
 
• Efforts to reduce fiscal deficits include increasing revenue through taxes and reducing unnecessary expenditures.
 
 
 
• **Budgetary Allocation**
 
 
• Budgetary Allocation refers to the distribution of financial resources among various sectors and departments of the government.
 
• It is a crucial aspect of the government's budget, determining how funds will be utilized over the fiscal year.
 
• Proper budgetary allocation ensures optimal utilization of resources and effective implementation of government policies and programs.
 
• It involves prioritizing sectors such as health, education, infrastructure, defense, and social welfare based on current needs and goals.

questions.question: Which one of the following is called the ‘digestive bag’ in the cell ?
questions.solution:
**__Concept:__**

__
 
• Eukaryotic cells contain distinct nuclei as well as double membrane-bound cell organelles.
 
• The membranous organelles namely the endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi complex, lysosomes, and vacuoles are considered together as an endomembrane system because their functions are coordinated.
 
• While other membranous organelles like mitochondria, plastids, peroxisomes, etc. are distinct in terms of their structures as well as functions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• **Lysosomes are called the ‘digestive bag’ in the cell**.
 
• These are membrane-bound vesicular structures formed by the process of packaging in the Golgi apparatus.
 
• **Lysosomes are very rich in almost all types of hydrolytic enzymes, viz., lipases, proteases, carbohydrases**, etc.
 
• **These enzymes are able to digest carbohydrates, lipids, proteins, nucleic acids, etc**. 
 
• These also** digest and remove the wear and tear organelles **and **molecules from the cell**. 
 
• The hydrolase enzymes of lysosomes are optimally active at the acidic pH.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****Golgi body-**

 
• ​These are the double membrane-bound cell organelles that principally perform the functions of packaging materials, to be delivered either to the intra-cellular targets or secreted outside the cells.
 
• It is an important site for the formation of glycoproteins and glycolipids.

**Mitochondria-**

 
• This is a sausage-shaped or cylindrical cell organelle having a double membrane.
 
• Mitochondria are the sites of aerobic respiration.
 
• They produce cellular energy in the form of ATP, thus they are called the 'Power house' of the cell.

**Ribosome-**

 
• Ribosomes are the granular structures that are scattered in the cytoplasm or attached to the endoplasmic reticulum forming Rough endoplasmic reticulum.
 
• These are actively associated with protein synthesis and secretion.
 
• Ribosomes are known as the 'Protein factory' of cells.
 
• They are composed of ribonucleic acids and proteins and are not surrounded by any membrane.

**Hence the correct option is (4) Lysosomes.**

questions.question:
Consider the following statements :

1. Under Akbar, the system of Zabt was established over a large area from Punjab to Awadh.

2. In the seventeenth century North India, the system of Zabt lost much ground to the system of Kankut.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__1 only.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Zabt System**

 
 
• The** Zabt System or Dahsala System** was introduced by **Raja Todarmal.**
 
• He was** Akbar's competent finance minister.**
 
• Under the reign of Akbar, he performed his **duty in Agra** and later **served as the governor of Gujarat.**
 
• This system introduces in the **year 1580-82 to put a check on the problems **that were arising due to fixing prices each year and revenue settlement of the last year.
 
• Under the Dahsala or Zabti System, there were** no ten years of settlement on the crops.**
 
• It was** based on the average prices and produces during the last ten years.**
 
• This system was basically in practice during Shershah Suri but was honed **perfectly during Akbar’s reign.**
 
• The system of Zabt **did not apply to the provinces of Gujarat and West Bengal** because in those areas the rulers of the Mughal empire were not able to keep the data and track the records of

 the revenue system.
 
• This system was **applied in northern India **and in Malwa and parts of Gujarat. 
 
• The **main provinces **covered under the Zabt system were **Delhi, Allahabad, Awadh, Agra, Lahore and Multan. *Hence statement 1 is correct.***
 
 
 
• In **Malikzada's Nigamama-i Munshi (late 17th century)** crop sharing has been mentioned as the **best method of revenue assessment and collection. ***Hence statement 2 is incorrect.*
 
• Under thismethod, the** peasants and the state shared the risks of the seasons equally.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Kankut system**

 
 
• In Kankut or appraisement, the **whole land was measured,** either by using the jarib or pacing it, and the **standing crops estimated by inspection.**
 
• It was also known as **Danabandi.**
 
• It was also an **old prevalent method** in which, instead of **actually dividing the grain (kan), an estimate (kut) **was made on the basis of an actual inspection on the spot and **one-third of the estimated produce was fixed as the state demand.* ***
 
• So, it was a** rough estimate** of produce on the basis of actual inspection and past experience.​

questions.question: The total pressure of a mixture of ideal gases is the sum of partial pressures. This is ______ law of partial pressures.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 1**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• This is known as Dalton's law of partial pressures.
 
• According to Dalton's law, the total pressure exerted by a mixture of non-reacting ideal gases is equal to the sum of the partial pressures of each individual gas.
 
• Dalton's law is based on the assumption that the gases in the mixture behave independently of one another, without any significant interactions or reactions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Boyle's Law:**

 
 
• Boyle's law states that, at a constant temperature, the volume of a given amount of gas is inversely proportional to its pressure.
 
• In other words,** as the pressure of a gas increases, its volume decreases, and vice versa, provided the temperature remains constant.** Mathematically, Boyle's law can be expressed as:
 
• **P₁V₁ = P₂V₂**
 
• where** P₁ and V₁ **are the** initial pressure** and **volume**, and **P₂ and V₂** are the **final pressure and volume**, respectively.
 
 
 
• **Charles's Law:**
 
 
• **Charles's law** states that, at a constant pressure, the volume of a given amount of gas is directly proportional to its absolute temperature. This means that as the temperature of a gas increases, its volume also increases, and as the temperature decreases, its volume decreases, as long as the pressure remains constant. Mathematically, Charles's law can be expressed as:
 
• **V₁/T₁ = V₂/T₂**
 
• where **V₁ and T₁ **are the initial **volume and temperature (in Kelvin), **and** V₂ and T₂ **are the **final volume and temperature**, respectively.
 
 
 
• **Avogadro's Law:**
 
 
• **Avogadro's law states** that, at a constant temperature and pressure, equal volumes of gases contain an equal number of particles (atoms, molecules, or ions).
 
• This law implies that the volume of a gas is directly proportional to the number of moles of gas present. Mathematically, Avogadro's law can be expressed as:
 
• **V₁/n₁ = V₂/n₂**
 
 

where** V₁ and n₁ **are the** initial volume** and number of** moles**, and **V₂ and n₂** are the **final volume **and number of **moles,** respectively.

questions.question: Which one of the following depicts correct demographic equation of population growth?
questions.solution:
**Population Growth** refers to a change in the size of a population. It can be either positive or negative over time. It is caused exclusively by the operation of **fertility, mortality, and migration. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** All populations change in size with time

__
 
• if births exceed deaths, the population grows
 
• if deaths exceed births, the population shrinks
 
• only when births equal deaths does the population stay the same

We can write a simple equation to show population growth as:

**Change in Population Size = (Births + Immigration) - (Deaths + Emigration)**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__** 

 
• The Natural Balance refers to the difference between the number of births and the number of deaths recorded over a period. When **the number of births is greater than that of deaths, it is called Natural increase**. 
 
• **Dependency Ratio **is a measure of the number of dependents aged zero to 14 and over the age of 65, compared with the total population aged 15 to 64. It tells about the number of non-working people, compared to the number of those of working age.
 
• **Net migration **refers to the difference between the number of **immigrants(people coming to a place)** and the **number of emigrants(people leaving an area)** throughout a given period.
 
• **In-Migration **is the process of people moving into a new area to live there permanently.
 
• **Out-Migration **is the process of people moving out of an area to move to another area permanently
 
• **Birth Rate** refers to the number of individuals born in a population in a given period of time. It is stated as the number of births per 1000 persons in a given year,
 
• **Death Rate **is the ratio of the number of deaths per thousand people in a given year. 

**Hence the correct Demographic equation of population growth is Natural increase and Net Migration.**
